item.title: Kadavu farmer turns challenges into innovation, prepares to represent Fiji and Pacific in China
item.description: A 31-year-old farmer from Kadavu who experienced first-hand the challenges facing smallholder farmers, taught himself technology and built his own solution, is now preparing to represent Fiji and the Pacific at a global agriculture innovation competition in China. item.content:encoded:
A 31-year-old farmer from Kadavu who experienced first-hand the challenges facing smallholder farmers, taught himself technology and built his own solution, is now preparing to represent Fiji and the Pacific at a global agriculture innovation competition in China.

Uraia Koroi Kama of Solodamu, Tavuki in Kadavu is the founder of Teivaka, an agriculture platform developed from his own experiences and the challenges he saw farmers facing.

Koroi Kama was studying for a science degree at the University of the South Pacific, majoring in mathematics and physics, when he decided to leave university and pursue his passion for farming, something he says he had loved since childhood.

After more than seven years as a farmer, Koroi Kama says he began questioning why people could spend their whole lives farming, but still struggle to grow their businesses or have little to show for decades of work.

He says farmers face challenges accessing knowledge, managing their farms, building connections and securing finance, while their years of farming experience are often not formally recognised when they approach institutions such as banks.

These challenges led him to develop Teivaka, an online platform designed to connect farmers with buyers, suppliers, agribusinesses, trainers, institutions and others involved in agriculture.

The platform also aims to help farmers manage their farms, access agricultural knowledge and build a record of their farming activities that could support their dealings with banks, buyers and other institutions.

However, Koroi Kama says turning his idea into a working platform was far from easy, as he had no technology background and had to teach himself from the basics.

He says the project was funded through income from his two pilot farms, together with support from his family and a few close friends.

At one stage, Koroi Kama says he considered giving up after spending thousands of dollars with little to show for it.

He says it took 262 versions and more than 2,000 hours of work to reach a working prototype, with much of the development done at night after spending the day working on the farm.

Koroi Kama says getting only four hours of sleep became normal as he balanced farming, family expenses and developing Teivaka.

His persistence eventually gained national recognition when Teivaka became one of the winners of the Agri Innovate competition in June.

The platform has now been selected as one of 13 finalists from 137 entries across 50 countries for a global agriculture innovation competition in China.

Koroi Kama says it took time for him to process that something developed on a small island in Kadavu would now compete on a global stage.

He says he is not going to China only for Teivaka, but to represent Fiji's farmers and the wider Pacific.

Koroi Kama says simply reaching the global stage is already a major opportunity, as it could put Teivaka in front of people who understand and invest in agricultural innovation.

He is also encouraging young Fijians with business ideas to start by identifying problems in areas they are passionate about and finding ways to solve them.

Koroi Kama says the journey will not be easy, but skills can be learnt if people are willing to ask questions, find answers and put in the work.

item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Barisal, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: Yaqona Bill to undergo further public consultation
item.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Waterways says further public consultations will be held through the Parliamentary Standing Committee process, despite national consultations on the proposed legislation already being conducted from February to May this year. The Ministry says it acknowledges the strong public interest and concerns raised about the Bill following its tabling in Parliament on August
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Agriculture and Waterways says further public consultations will be held through the Parliamentary Standing Committee process, despite national consultations on the proposed legislation already being conducted from February to May this year.

The Ministry says it acknowledges the strong public interest and concerns raised about the Bill following its tabling in Parliament on August 21st.

It stresses that no final decision has been made and the Bill remains proposed legislation.

Following its First Reading, the Bill has been referred to the relevant Parliamentary Standing Committee for further review.

The Ministry says the Standing Committee process will include further public consultations, before the Bill can proceed to its Second and Third Readings in Parliament.

It is encouraging yaqona farmers, growers, traders, processors, exporters and other members of the public to take part in the consultations and provide their views and recommendations.

The Ministry says public participation is important as thousands of households across Fiji depend on the yaqona industry for their livelihoods.

item.description: A 41-year-old man and his 35-year-old wife are in custody after Police say they were found with white powder believed to be illicit drugs and burglary tools in their vehicle in Dokanaisuva. Police say t he couple were stopped and their vehicle was checked at a checkpoint at around 1am yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
A 41-year-old man and his 35-year-old wife are in custody after Police say they were found with white powder believed to be illicit drugs and burglary tools in their vehicle in Dokanaisuva.

Police say t he couple were stopped and their vehicle was checked at a checkpoint at around 1am yesterday.

They say the vehicle had an expired wheel tax and the man, who was driving, did not have a valid drivers licence.

The couple remains in custody as Police investigations continue.

item.title: Changes in a child’s behaviour could be a sign they are struggling – Naisele
item.description: Substance Abuse Advisory Council Director Josua Naisele says children do not always communicate their problems through words, and changes in their behaviour can also be a way of showing that something is wrong. Naisele says repeatedly coming home late, not doing homework or suddenly changing friends could indicate that something is happening in a child's life.
item.content:encoded:
Substance Abuse Advisory Council Director Josua Naisele says children do not always communicate their problems through words, and changes in their behaviour can also be a way of showing that something is wrong.

Naisele says repeatedly coming home late, not doing homework or suddenly changing friends could indicate that something is happening in a child's life.

He says rather than immediately becoming angry, parents should try to understand what may be behind the change in behaviour.

Naisele says children need someone who will listen to them and make an effort to understand what they are going through.

He says when a child approaches a parent wanting to share something, parents should put other things aside, give the child their full attention and listen.

Naisele says when children do not receive enough attention at home, they may instead turn to friends or other people who are willing to listen to them.

He says building a strong connection at home can make children feel more comfortable approaching their parents when they are facing problems.

Naisele also urges parents to be mindful of how they speak when correcting their children.

He says when parents shout, children may focus more on the tone being used than on the message the parent is trying to get across.

Naisele says parents should communicate calmly, listen to their children and spend quality time with them to create a home environment where children feel safe and comfortable speaking openly about what they are going through.

item.title: Two new care model homes receive furnishings for vulnerable elderly residents
item.description: Two new care model homes at Koroipita Model Town have received furnishings and are now ready to welcome elderly residents who do not have a safe place to stay. Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran officiated at the handing over of the furnishings provided by LDS Charities for the newly built units.
item.content:encoded:
Two new care model homes at Koroipita Model Town have received furnishings and are now ready to welcome elderly residents who do not have a safe place to stay.

Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran officiated at the handing over of the furnishings provided by LDS Charities for the newly built units.

Kiran says the homes will provide full-time, around-the-clock care for elderly residents who require support and have limited options for safe accommodation.

Koroipita Model Town General Manager Paul Forrester says the community now has more than 1,500 residents, including 62 people in their 60s and 27 people aged over 70.

He says the growing number of elderly residents highlights the need for aged care services within the community, particularly for people who have experienced hardship.

Forrester says the two homes are Koroipita’s first step towards providing full-time care for elderly residents.

He says the facilities will provide residents with companionship, improved care and support, while also addressing their nutritional and sanitation needs.

Kiran says Fiji has not paid enough attention to ageing over the past two decades and Government is now working to address the growing need for care services for older people.

She says Government’s existing HPL facilities are fully occupied, making community-based care an important option.

K iran says the Koroipita care model homes will allow elderly residents to receive care while remaining connected to the wider community.

She thanked Koroipita’s management, board and trustees for supporting the development of the facilities, and LDS Charities for providing the furnishings.

The first residents are expected to move into the new homes next week.
